formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the allowance of `spender` over the owner's bridged USDC (USDC.e on Arbitrum) to exactly `value`. It replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it.
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce, so any other pending permit signed with that nonce becomes invalid.
The signature only works until `deadline` (block.timestamp <= deadline). After that, permit reverts.
formats.shown: The intent "Authorize spending of tokens" is shown, then the spender as a raw address, the maximum amount in USDC.e ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the expiry date and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit format has no test case, so neither the normal rendering nor the "Unlimited" threshold is tested.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: "cases: 0 (no tx)" for Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline). descriptor.json value field: "threshold": "0x8000…", "message": "Unlimited".
findings.fix: Add EIP-712 test cases for Permit on 42161:0xff970a61a04b1ca14834a43f5de4533ebddb5cc8. Use one finite value (for example 100 USDC.e) and one value of type(uint256).max that shows "Unlimited".

findings.title: Permit intent does not name the token, and there is no interpolated intent to name the spender or amount.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", interpolatedIntent absent. ArbFiatToken.permit -> ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit: _approve(owner, spender, value).
findings.fix: Optionally change the intent to "Approve USDC.e spending". Add an interpolatedIntent like "Approve {spender} to spend {value}".
